article.title: Loopyah推出AI廣告管理，以售票結帳資料調整跨平台預算
article.title_en: Loopyah launches AI ads management tied to ticket-checkout results
article.summary: 澳洲售票平台Loopyah公布AI Ads Manager，使用Claude及Amazon Bedrock管理Meta、Google及TikTok廣告。
article.summary_en: Australian ticketing platform Loopyah announced an AI Ads Manager using Claude and Amazon Bedrock across Meta, Google and TikTok.
highlights: 主辦方連接廣告帳戶、設定預算，活動結束日須在3至30日後。
系統按平台結帳售票資料調整投放，並以文字記錄變更及原因。
highlights_en: Organizers connect ad accounts and set a budget with an end date 3 to 30 days away.
The system uses its checkout sales to adjust delivery and logs changes and reasons.
article.why: 售票團隊可用同一結帳訊號檢視跨渠道預算分配，決定是否讓系統把支出移向帶來售票的平台。
article.why_en: Event teams can assess cross-channel allocation against one checkout signal before allowing budget to move between platforms.
article.next_step: 以一場活動列清售票目標、總預算及結束日，逐日比對售票記錄與系統變更日誌，再決定是否擴大接入渠道。
article.next_step_en: Set ticket goals, budget and end date for one event, then reconcile daily sales with change logs before adding channels.
article.detail: 消息來自Loopyah發布的付費新聞稿，並非獨立投放測試。公司表示主辦方可暫停個別或全部活動，廣告費直接付予平台，Loopyah不另加廣告支出費用。系統以自有結帳資料作調整依據，與單靠各廣告平台回報的轉換不同。這項機制不等於已證明增量銷售或改善廣告回報，團隊應把變更記錄與實際售票逐筆對照。
article.detail_en: This is a paid issuer release, not an independent campaign test. Loopyah says organizers can pause campaigns and pay platforms directly without an ad-spend markup. Its checkout signal differs from relying only on platform conversions. That mechanism does not prove incremental ticket sales or improved return; reconcile logs with actual transactions.
